scope: Publicly discoverable Koan skill listings, catalog copies, registry packages, and install or download surfaces associated with the retired granular and first-generation skill sets.

methodology.verifiedListing: An exact public URL or public registry API record was observed during the investigation. Search-result evidence is identified when the destination itself was not directly inspectable.
methodology.candidateAlias: A name follows a platform's observed naming convention or was seen in earlier coverage, but its exact public URL could not be revalidated. Candidates are not counted as verified listings.
methodology.consumerEvidence: An install, download, export, or repository-fetch instruction proves that a listing can distribute legacy content; it does not prove that a third party installed or used it.
methodology.usageSignal: Stars, forks, quality scores, and views are recorded only with their platform meaning and are not converted into install counts.

sourceRepository.disposition: Publish and index only the three canonical skills. Legacy loader paths are removed; retain their identities only in non-loader historical inventory and migration records.

mirrorInvestigation.evidence: Direct public repository pages and unauthenticated GitHub tree API responses verified six repositories containing at least 36 copied directories, files, or snapshots of retired Koan skills.
limits: GitHub's recursive tree response is truncated for the two very large majiayu000 registry repositories; their listed paths are exact verified minimums rather than a complete copy count.
Repository presence and copied files do not prove invocation or active use.
Ordinary forks that do not independently publish copied paths were not counted as listings.
mirrorInvestigation.followUp: Ask each owner to purge by upstream source URL and historical blob fingerprints; re-enumerate the two generated registries through their operator APIs to close the truncated-tree count.

knownConsumerEvidence.interpretation: All twelve public pages offered repository-archive distribution; the observed install counters were zero.
At least two verified MCPMarket pages could direct a consumer to install a retired repository skill.

Three legacy packages remained publicly available and not deprecated at verification time; their reported counters were zero.
The page had visible exposure and an install path, but no verified install count.
A rated legacy performance listing remained installable; the rating is not evidence of use.
The legacy MCP skill remained discoverable through a public index.
A downstream application repository contains four retired Koan skills under its active .agents/skills path; this proves installation/copying, not invocation.

globalDisposition.repository: Make .agents/skills the sole canonical source, remove legacy loader entrypoints, and preserve legacy identities only in non-loader retirement and inventory records.
globalDisposition.marketplaces: Delist every legacy listing and candidate alias; where removal is impossible, mark it deprecated and point to the canonical manifest.
globalDisposition.replacement: Publish only koan, koan-explain, and koan-upgrade, each from its canonical .agents/skills directory.
globalDisposition.verification: After operator actions, repeat exact-URL checks, repository-identity searches, and install-path checks; record action receipts separately from this pre-action evidence ledger.
